app_info.subtitle: Use local secrets safely
app_info.description: KeepKeys brokers local credential use through the operating-system vault, native approval windows, and one-time private phone intake without returning plaintext secrets to ChatGPT.

justifications.read_only_justification: Stores a user-supplied credential in the local operating-system vault after the user completes the native Paste & Store action.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only changes the private vault on the user's device and does not write to public internet state or a third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can overwrite the named local credential, while the native Store window keeps the value outside ChatGPT and requires an explicit user action.

justifications.read_only_justification: Accepts a user paste through a one-time private Tailscale Serve page and stores it in the local operating-system vault.
justifications.open_world_justification: The page is tailnet-only and writes only to the user's local vault; it does not use a public relay or publish external state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can overwrite the named local credential, with one-use expiry, tailnet access control, and an explicit Paste & Store action before the write.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists friendly names and non-secret metadata without reading protected credential values.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only local metadata and does not write to public internet state or a third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke, or otherwise change a credential.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reopens the native Paste & Store flow to replace one named local credential after the user provides the replacement outside ChatGPT.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only changes the private local vault and does not write to public internet state or a third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the existing credential and clears its exact-command automatic approval rules before accepting the replacement.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes automatic approval rules after native confirmation without reading or changing the protected credential value.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only local approval policy and does not write to public internet state or a third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: It disables convenience rules but does not delete the credential or revoke an external account.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes one named local credential only after the user confirms the native destructive confirmation window.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only changes the private local vault and does not write to public internet state or a third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes the selected local credential and its metadata, and the deletion cannot be recovered by KeepKeys.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs a user-approved direct executable with one scoped environment variable and returns only bounded, redacted output.
justifications.open_world_justification: The approved executable may contact external services or change external state, so the user must review its exact path, arguments, purpose, and fingerprint.
justifications.destructive_justification: A user-approved command can change local or external state; KeepKeys rejects shells, uses an empty child environment, and requires native approval.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reports local helper availability and vault capability without reading or changing credentials.
justifications.open_world_justification: Inspects only local platform state and does not contact or modify public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create, update, delete, revoke, or execute a credential-bearing command.

justifications.read_only_justification: Performs a temporary generated-value vault round trip and deletes the generated test record before returning.
justifications.open_world_justification: The generated test is local and does not write to public internet state or a third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: It does not touch a user credential; the temporary generated record is explicitly cleaned up.

test_cases.description: Store a credential outside ChatGPT through the native vault flow.
test_cases.user_prompt: Store a new synthetic demo credential for the approved demo-service request using DEMO_API_TOKEN.
test_cases.expected_output: The agent researches an official provider documentation URL, sends metadata only, and directs the user to the native Paste & Store action. The result confirms storage without returning the value.

test_cases.description: Accept a credential from a phone without public hosting.
test_cases.user_prompt: Set up phone intake for a synthetic phone-demo credential using PHONE_DEMO_TOKEN.
test_cases.expected_output: The agent returns one expiring tailnet-only HTTPS link without opening it. The user pastes on the authenticated phone page, and the page closes after the native vault write.

test_cases.description: Inspect metadata and verify local readiness.
test_cases.user_prompt: List my KeepKeys entries, check availability, and run the generated-value vault doctor.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns names and non-secret metadata, local platform status, and doctor cleanup status without returning any protected value.

test_cases.description: Use, rotate, and disable convenience approval for a credential.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use demo-service with the absolute curl executable for a local version check, then rotate it and disable its automatic approval rules.
test_cases.expected_output: The user reviews exact native command approval before execution. Rotation reopens Paste & Store and clears old exact-command rules; revocation reports how many rules were removed.

test_cases.description: Remove a credential after native confirmation.
test_cases.expected_output: A native destructive confirmation is shown, and the result reports deletion without exposing the protected value.

negative_test_cases.description: Reject a plaintext credential pasted into chat.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Here is my token: [fresh synthetic value]. Save it for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app does not pass or repeat the value. It explains that the user must press Paste & Store in native UI or on the one-time tailnet page.

negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the value of demo-service.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app refuses because it has no get, reveal, copy, export, or secret-returning workflow, and offers approved use or removal instead.

negative_test_cases.description: Reject environment dumps and shell execution.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Use demo-service with /usr/bin/env, or cmd.exe /c set on Windows, so I can see whether it loaded.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app does not invoke an environment dump or shell and explains that KeepKeys accepts only a direct executable that does not print its scoped credential.
